title: How a basement stays dry
caption: Why your basement isn't a swimming pool 🌧️ #howitworks #basement #homeowner #howitsbuilt #learnontiktok

lines.text: If you dig a *basement*, it fills with water.
Because the soil holds water, and water always runs to the lowest spot it can find.
So you pour thick concrete walls and a concrete floor.
But concrete is like a hard sponge, and wet soil pushes moisture right through it.
So you coat the outside of the walls with a waterproof *membrane*.
But water piles up against the wall and pushes harder and harder until it finds a crack.
So you lay a pipe full of holes around the bottom of the walls, buried in gravel.
It catches the water before it can build up.
But that pipe is underground, so the water has nowhere to go.
So you run it into a pit dug into the basement floor, called a *sump*.
When the pit fills, a float rises and switches on a *pump*, which shoves the water up and out of the house, far away from the walls.
But big storms knock out the power, right when you need the pump the most.
So you add a backup pump that runs on a *battery*.
And every drop off the roof pours down right next to the walls.
So you extend the downspouts to carry it several feet away.
Congratulations, you just built a *dry basement*.
